verses.text: Then he brought me into the main hall of the temple and measured its side pillars. They were six cubits wide on each side.
The entrance was ten cubits wide, and the walls on each side of it were five cubits wide. He measured the main hall. It was forty cubits long and twenty cubits wide.
Then he went into the inner room and measured the side pillars of its entrance. Each was two cubits thick. The entrance was six cubits wide, and the walls on each side of it were seven cubits wide.
He measured the inner room at the far end of the main hall. It was twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. He said to me, "This is the Most Holy Place."
Then he measured the wall of the temple. It was six cubits thick. Each of the side rooms all around the temple was four cubits wide.

The side rooms were built in three levels, one above the other, thirty rooms on each level. They rested on ledges in the temple wall all around, so that they were supported without being fastened into the wall itself.

The side rooms got wider on each higher level, because the wall got narrower as it went up. So the building became wider toward the top, and a stairway went up from the lowest level through the middle level to the highest.
I saw that the temple had a raised base all around it. This formed the foundation of the side rooms, and it was a full rod of six long cubits high.
The outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits thick. There was an open space between the side rooms of the temple
and the priests' rooms. It was twenty cubits wide all around the temple.
The side rooms had doors opening onto the open space, one door on the north and another on the south. The open space was five cubits wide all around.
The building facing the temple courtyard on the west side was seventy cubits wide. Its wall was five cubits thick all around, and it was ninety cubits long.
Then he measured the temple. It was one hundred cubits long. The temple courtyard and the building with its walls were also one hundred cubits long.
The front of the temple, along with the courtyard on the east, was one hundred cubits wide.

He measured the length of the building facing the courtyard at the back of the temple, including its galleries on each side. It was one hundred cubits. The main hall, the inner room, and the porches facing the courtyard,

along with the thresholds, the narrow windows, and the galleries on all three levels, were all covered with wood paneling. The paneling went from the floor up to the windows, and the windows were covered.
The space above the entrance, the inner room, the outside, and all the walls all around, inside and out, were measured.
The walls were decorated with cherubim and palm trees. A palm tree stood between each pair of cherubim. Each cherub had two faces:
the face of a man turned toward the palm tree on one side, and the face of a young lion turned toward the palm tree on the other side. These were carved all around the whole temple.
Cherubim and palm trees were carved from the floor to the space above the entrance, on the wall of the main hall.
The doorposts of the main hall were square. In front of the Most Holy Place was something that looked
like an altar made of wood. It was three cubits high and two cubits long. Its corners, its base, and its sides were made of wood. The man said to me, "This is the table that stands before the LORD."
The main hall and the Most Holy Place each had a double door.
Each door had two leaves that swung on hinges, two leaves for one door and two for the other.
Cherubim and palm trees were carved on the doors of the main hall, like those carved on the walls. There was a wooden roof over the front of the porch outside.
There were narrow windows with palm trees carved on each side of the porch. This is how the side rooms of the temple and the roofs were made.
